34875-spain.title: Spain
34875-spain.creator: Unknown
34875-spain.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. The ordinary descriptions of Spain present only one, or at most two, types, the Castling and Andalusian, and utterly neglect all the rest. The provinces of Spain have been well described as divided into "five Irelands" whose habits and modes of thought, political aspirations, and commercial interests and aptitudes, are often utterly opposed to those of the capital.

arxiv-2111-12379.title: Efficient Anomaly Detection Using Self-Supervised Multi-Cue Tasks
arxiv-2111-12379.creator: Loïc Jézéquel, Ngoc-Son Vu, Jean Beaudet, and Aymeric Histace
arxiv-2111-12379.description: Abstract Anomaly detection is important in many real-life applications. Recently, self-supervised learning has greatly helped deep anomaly detection by recognizing several geometric transformations. However these methods lack finer features, usually highly depend on the anomaly type, and do not perform well on fine-grained problems.

arxiv-2204-09716.title: Domain Specific Fine-tuning of Denoising Sequence-to-Sequence Models for Natural Language Summarization
arxiv-2204-09716.creator: Brydon Parker Alik Sokolov Mahtab Ahmed Matt Kalebic, Sedef Akinli Kocak Ofer Shai
arxiv-2204-09716.description: Abstract Summarization of long-form text data is a problem especially pertinent in knowledge economy jobs such as medicine and finance, that require continuously remaining informed on a sophisticated and evolving body of knowledge. As such, isolating and summarizing key content automatically using Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques holds the potential for extensive time savings in these industries.

pmc-10650699.title: MLH1 Methylation Testing as an Integral Component of Universal Endometrial Cancer Screening—A Critical Appraisal
pmc-10650699.creator: Anna Plotkin, Ekaterina Olkhov-Mitsel, Sharon Nofech-Mozes, Carmela De Marco
pmc-10650699.description: Simple SummaryOften in endometrial cancer (EC), the mismatch repair (MMR) system, which helps fix DNA mistakes, goes haywire because of MLH1 promoter hypermethylation (MLH1-PHM). We set out to find out how many ECs have MLH1-PHM, understand the impact of reflex MLH1-PHM testing and evaluate the associated costs within the publicly funded Canadian healthcare system.

pmc-11645119.title: Dietary pattern transition and its nutrient intakes and diet quality among Japanese population: results from the 2003–2019 National Survey
pmc-11645119.creator: Yui Sakai, Yen Yen Sally Rahayu, Yajie Zhao, Tetsuya Araki
pmc-11645119.description: Objective:While many Asian countries undergo dietary transitions, little is known about Japan’s dietary pattern changes and their impact on nutritional intake. We aimed to examine 17-year trends in dietary patterns and nutrient intakes in Japan.Design:Principal component analysis was used to derive dietary patterns.

pmc-12088175.title: Outcomes of Operative Management of Multi-Ligament Knee Injuries in an Adolescent Population: A Retrospective Case Series
pmc-12088175.creator: Pamela J Lang, Aliya Feroe, Helena Franco, Zaamin B Hussain, Frances A Tepolt, Mininder S Kocher
pmc-12088175.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background: Multi-ligament knee injuries in adolescent patients are rare. The aim of this study was to describe the presentation, surgical management, and patient outcomes following multi-ligament knee injuries in an adolescent cohort.Methods: A retrospective case series was conducted involving all patients aged ≤18 years who underwent surgery for a multi-ligament knee injury at a single institution between March 2005 and January 2015.

pmc-12541395.title: Inequality in air pollution–attributable mortality by income level between and within countries
pmc-12541395.creator: Chenliang Tao, Yuqiang Zhang, Drew Shindell, Hongliang Zhang
pmc-12541395.description: SignificanceAir pollution is one of the leading causes of adverse health impacts worldwide, particularly in low- and middle-income countries with high exposure levels. However, impacts within countries are also uneven, being influenced by local factors, including exposures. This paper assesses premature mortality disparities across different income groups between and within countries.

pmc-13100847.title: Dynamic inflammatory trajectories and 28-day mortality in patients in the intensive care unit: An exploratory observational study
pmc-13100847.creator: Xinyuan Ding, Shangzhong Chen, Lihong Zhu, Chengcheng Zheng, Hang Mou, Guolong Cai, Yanfei Shen
pmc-13100847.description: Highlights•Early inflammatory trajectories strongly predict 28-day mortality in ICU patients.•Sustained high inflammation (Traj. 3) is linked to the highest mortality risk.•Multi-indicator trajectory predicts immune stability and 28-day mortality risk.•Vasopressors and steroids benefit high-inflammation states. Steroids worsen outcomes in those who rapidly develop high inflammatory states.•Traj. 3 marks early high-risk; Day 9 is a risk node, needing early intervention.

pmc-13116853.title: The Association Between Soil Sampling and Bait Traps in Wireworm Monitoring: A Methodological and Statistical Approach
pmc-13116853.creator: Lorenzo Furlan, Giancarlo Bourlot, Annalisa Turchi, Valerio Snichelotto, Maddalena Cappello Fusaro, Stefano Bona
pmc-13116853.description: Simple SummaryWireworms are soil-dwelling insect larvae that may cause damage to crops such as maize, potatoes and sunflower. Environment-harmful insecticides have been and are being used widely to control wireworm populations. As wireworms live underground, they are difficult to detect, making it challenging for farmers to decide when control measures are really needed.
